'''Armed conflicts and attacks'''
*[[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]]
**[[Siege of Mariupol]]
***Ukrainian authorities say that about 200 dead people are found in the rubble of an apartment building in [[Mariupol]], [[Donetsk Oblast]]. [https://apnews.com/article/russia-ukraine-zelenskyy-kyiv-0c74a0c16b834732b81e460450da3131 (AP)]
**[[Battle of Donbas (2022)|Battle of Donbas]]
***[[Russian Ground Forces]] seize control of [[Svitlodarsk]] in [[Donetsk Oblast]], according to regional governor [[Pavlo Kyrylenko]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/eu-oil-embargo-in-days-ukraine-isolation-drives-russia-closer-china-2022-05-23/ (Reuters)]
**[[Hungary]] declares a [[state of emergency]] over the [[2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine|war in Ukraine]] and problems in the [[Hungarian economy]] caused in part by the conflict. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/hungarys-government-gets-emergency-powers-due-ukraine-war-pm-orban-says-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[War on drugs]]
**[[Mexican drug war]]
***[[Celaya massacre]]
****Eleven people are killed during a [[mass shooting]] at a hotel in [[Celaya]], [[Guanajuato]], [[Mexico]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/least-11-killed-central-mexico-apparent-gangland-attack-media-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Vila Cruzeiro shootout]]
***Twenty-one people are killed in a [[shootout]] between [[Brazil]]ian police and the [[Comando Vermelho]] gang in a [[favela]] in [[Rio de Janeiro]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/americas/eleven-dead-police-raid-drug-traffickers-rio-de-janeiro-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Kashmir conflict]]
**[[Insurgency in Jammu and Kashmir]]
***An [[India]]n policeman is killed and his seven-year-old daughter injured in an attack in [[Srinagar]], [[Jammu and Kashmir (union territory)|Jammu and Kashmir]]. [https://www.thehindu.com/news/national/policeman-killed-daughter-injured-in-srinagar-militant-attack/article65457101.ece (''The Hindu'')]
*[[Kurdish–Turkish conflict (1978–present)|Kurdish–Turkish conflict]]
**[[Operation Claw-Lock]]
***Five [[Turkish soldier]]s are killed by [[Kurd]]ish fighters in [[Iraq]]. [https://english.alaraby.co.uk/news/five-turkish-soldiers-killed-iraq-defence-ministry (''The New Arab'')]
*[[Yemeni Civil War (2014–present)|Yemeni Civil War]]
**Three people are killed when a [[unmanned combat aerial vehicle|drone]] is shot down and crashes in [[Sanaa]], [[Yemen]]. [https://apnews.com/article/politics-houthis-yemen-middle-east-civil-wars-452d41adaadb69962ddf5088577d8b84 (AP)]
*[[Israeli–Palestinian conflict]]
**An independent investigation by [[CNN]], aided by a newly released video by fellow [[Al Jazeera Media Network|Al Jazeera]] correspondent, points to late journalist [[Shireen Abu Akleh]] having been deliberately targeted by [[Israeli Defense Forces|IDF]] soldiers. [https://www.cnn.com/2022/05/24/middleeast/shireen-abu-akleh-jenin-killing-investigation-cmd-intl/index.html (CNN)]

'''Business and economy'''
*[[2019–present Sri Lankan economic crisis]], [[Economy of Sri Lanka]]
**[[Sri Lanka]] increases fuel prices in order to help public finances and combat a debilitating economic crisis. Acting [[Prime Minister of Sri Lanka|Prime Minister]] [[Ranil Wickremesinghe]] warns that "there is a possibility that inflation will increase further". [https://www.channelnewsasia.com/asia/sri-lanka-increases-fuel-prices-combat-economic-crisis-2703361 (CNA)]
*[[Economic impact of the 2022 Russian invasion of Ukraine]], [[International sanctions during the Russo-Ukrainian War]]
**The [[United States Department of Treasury]] announces that it will not renew the sanctions exemption which permits Russia to service its sovereign debt to American investors. Allowing the exemption to expire increases the likelihood that Russia will default on that debt this summer. [https://www.wsj.com/articles/treasury-to-block-u-s-investors-from-receiving-russian-debt-payments-11653420533 (''The Wall Street Journal'')]
*[[Collective action in the United Kingdom]]
**The [[National Union of Rail, Maritime and Transport Workers]] votes to go on a [[general strike|national strike]] in the [[United Kingdom]] for the first time since 1994 after demanding a "decent pay rise, job security and no compulsory redundancies". [https://www.bbc.co.uk/news/uk-61573206 (BBC News)]

'''Disasters and accidents'''
*Several people are injured when a [[train collides]] with a bus in [[Blaustein]], [[Baden-Württemberg]], [[Germany]]. [https://apnews.com/article/germany-accidents-85f49f6a61446b87538be727bc4ee294 (AP)]
*Two pilots are killed in [[Isfahan]], [[Iran]], when their [[fighter jet]] crashes. [https://www.reuters.com/world/middle-east/two-iranian-pilots-killed-after-f7-jet-crashes-irna-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*Sixteen people are killed when a boat sinks off the coast of [[Myanmar]]. [https://apnews.com/article/bangladesh-myanmar-government-and-politics-accidents-religion-fdc3963f6b2f21223131e6a260786270 (AP)]

'''Health and environment'''
*[[COVID-19 pandemic]]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in Asia]]
***[[COVID-19 pandemic in India]]
****[[COVID-19 pandemic in Gujarat]]
*****[[Gujarat]] reports its first case of the [[SARS-CoV-2 Omicron variant#Sublineages and BA.2 subvariant|Omicron BA.5 variant]] in a person who traveled to [[South Africa]]. [https://www.thequint.com/amp/story/coronavirus/covid-coronavirus-ba5-variant-first-case-detected-gujarat-nri (The Quint)]
**[[COVID-19 pandemic in North Korea]]
***The [[Korean Central News Agency]] reports that [[North Korea]] has a total of 3 million suspected cases of [[COVID-19]]. [http://www.koreaherald.com/view.php?ud=20220524000138 (''Korea Herald'')]
*[[2022 monkeypox outbreak]]
**The [[Czech Republic]], [[Slovenia]], and the [[United Arab Emirates]] confirm their first cases of [[monkeypox]]. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/czech-republic-detects-its-first-case-monkeypox-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)] [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/slovenia-reports-first-case-monkeypox-infection-media-2022-05-24/ (Reuters 2)] [https://www.reuters.com/business/healthcare-pharmaceuticals/uae-announces-first-case-monkeypox-country-wam-2022-05-24/ (Reuters 3)]
**[[England]] reports 14 new cases of monkeypox, thereby bringing the total number of cases in the country to 70. [https://www.reuters.com/world/uk/england-detects-14-more-cases-monkeypox-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Federal Ministry of Health (Germany)|German Health Minister]] [[Karl Lauterbach]] announces that [[Germany]] has ordered 40,000 doses of the [[smallpox vaccine]] as a precaution, after the country reported its first case of monkeypox. [https://www.axios.com/2022/05/24/germany-orders-40k-smallpox-vaccines-after-reporting-monkeypox-cases (Axios)]
**[[Denmark]] announces that it will provide [[vaccine]]s produced by [[Bavarian Nordic]] to persons who have been in close contact with monkeypox cases. [https://www.reuters.com/world/europe/denmark-provide-vaccines-close-contacts-monkeypox-cases-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
**[[Lebanon]] reports its second suspected case of monkeypox. [https://www.beirut.com/l/63612 (Beirut)]

'''Law and crime'''
*[[Robb Elementary School shooting]]
**Nineteen children and two teachers are killed in a [[mass shooting]] at an elementary school in [[Uvalde, Texas|Uvalde]], [[Texas]], [[United States]]. The gunman, a local 18-year-old high school student, is subsequently killed by police. The gunman had also shot and critically wounded his grandmother earlier in the day. [https://abcnews.go.com/US/texas-elementary-school-reports-active-shooter-campus/story?id=84940951 (ABC News)]
*[[Media freedom in Russia]]
**The [[government of Russia|Russia]]n [[State Duma]] passes a bill that will allow state prosecutors to close Russian bureaus of media outlets from countries that Russia deems "unfriendly". The bill will now need to be passed by the upper house and receive President [[Putin]]'s signature. [https://www.reuters.com/business/media-telecom/russian-parliament-passes-bill-allowing-moscow-close-western-news-bureaus-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[2022 Pakistani protests]]
**A policeman is shot dead by a [[Pakistan Tehreek-e-Insaf]] official, leading to a police crackdown on pro-[[Imran Khan]] demonstrators. [https://www.reuters.com/world/asia-pacific/pakistan-bans-ousted-pm-khans-protest-march-after-policeman-killed-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*[[Uganda National Police|Ugandan police]] arrest veteran opposition politician [[Kizza Besigye]] for "inciting violence" and also disperse a crowd protesting against the government. [https://www.reuters.com/world/africa/uganda-arrests-oppositions-besigye-again-breaks-up-price-protests-2022-05-24/ (Reuters)]
*Anglo-Swiss [[commodity trading]] company [[Glencore]] pleads guilty to fraud charges related to bribery and [[price manipulation]] when pursuing preferential access to oil contracts. The company expects to pay total fines of $1.5 billion. [https://www.swissinfo.ch/eng/bloomberg/glencore-pleads-guilty-to-settle-sprawling-graft-probes/47620300 (Swissinfo)]
*Former [[President of Moldova]] [[Igor Dodon]] is arrested on charges including [[corruption]] and [[treason]]. [https://www.euronews.com/2022/05/24/igor-dodon-former-moldovan-president-arrested-on-suspicion-of-corruption (Euronews)]

'''Sports'''
*The [[Premier League]] approves the sale of [[Chelsea F.C.]] to a [[United States|U.S.]] [[consortium]] led by [[Los Angeles Dodgers]] co-owner [[Todd Boehly]]. Chelsea owner [[Roman Abramovich]] decided to sell the club after he was sanctioned over his connections to the [[Government of Russia|Russian government]]. [https://www.bbc.co.uk/sport/football/61490237 (BBC Sport)]
